How to plan holiday gifts on a budget

By Couple Better Gifts · Updated October 26, 2026 · How we choose gifts

Holiday shopping gets expensive when it happens one gift at a time with no overall plan. A simple list made in advance can keep spending under control and make each gift more thoughtful. You need three things: a total budget, a list of people, and a deadline for ordering.

Set a total, then divide it

Start with the amount you can spend in total, including wrapping, cards, and shipping. Then list each person and give them a share. Partners and close family may get a larger share; coworkers and neighbors a smaller one. Write the numbers down. When one gift costs more than planned, you can see where the difference comes from.

PersonBudgetIdeasOrder by
Partner$80Photo book, concert ticketsTwo weeks before
Parent$40Book by favorite author, coffeeTen days before
Sibling$30Card game, hobby suppliesTen days before
Coworker exchange$15Snacks, small plantOne week before

The amounts above are an example. Adjust them to your own budget.

Collect ideas before you shop

Spend a few minutes thinking about each person before you open a shopping site. What did they talk about this year? What did they start, finish, or lose? Write two or three ideas next to each name. Shopping with a list is faster and helps you avoid impulse buys. If you are stuck, the gift quiz can suggest a starting point based on their interests and your budget.

Order early

Shipping slows down in the weeks before major holidays, and popular items sell out. Personalized items need extra production time. Set your own deadline about two weeks before the holiday for anything shipped, and earlier for custom orders. Check each store’s posted holiday shipping cutoff dates.

Watch for real sales

Holiday sales can help, but a discount on something you did not plan to buy is not a saving. Compare the sale price to your list. Price tracking tools and store price histories can show whether a sale price is actually lower than usual. Buy early when you find a real deal on something already on your list.

Keep wrapping simple

Buy one roll of plain paper, one roll of ribbon, and a pack of tags for all your gifts. A consistent look appears intentional and costs less than many different papers. Reusable fabric bags or simple boxes can work for several years.

Before checkout

  • Compare each gift to the amount on your list.
  • Check the holiday shipping cutoff for every store.
  • Keep receipts and gift receipts together in one place.
